source.title: Mixture-of-Depths Attention
source.authors: Liang-Hui Zhu; Yuxin Fang; Ben-Cheng Liao; Shijie Wang; Tian-Heng Cheng; Zi-Long Huang; Chen Chen; Lai Wei; Yutao Zeng; Ya Wang; Yi Lin; Yu Li; Xing-Gang Wang

record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out validation perplexity at two parameter scales with the token budget held fixed, and compares some architecture variants at matched parameter counts. It does not fit or validate a scaling law.
record.gate_note: The reported 700M-to-1.5B validation-perplexity comparisons bear on loss changing with parameter count. The matched-parameter architecture comparisons bear on V4. Downstream task scores and kernel runtimes are not rows because they do not measure the loss-scaling laws in the claim.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper proposing MoDA. It cites Kaplan and Hoffmann only as motivation for depth scaling. Its 700M-vs-1.5B comparison checks whether MoDA's gains persist at a second size; it is not a test of how loss scales. Two sizes at one token budget cannot show a power-law form, an extrapolation or a compute-optimal split. The matched-parameter rows compare the authors' own mechanism against the OLMo2 baseline, which is a method-performance result rather than a test of whether model shape matters.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that MoDA gives consistent perplexity and downstream gains over OLMo2 at 700M and 1.5B, with about 3.7% extra FLOPs. They add that post-norm pairs better with MoDA than pre-norm, and that depth retrieval is a practical primitive for scaling depth. They make no scaling-law claim.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a new depth-attention architecture with OLMo2-style training; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported loss outcomes vary with architecture variant and, in the 48-layer experiments, normalization configuration; the paper notes larger Depth KV gains with post-norm than pre-norm.

fits_no_version.finding: At 48 layers and matched 123.38M parameters, pre-norm versus post-norm OLMo2 gives FineWeb-Edu validation loss 3.3800 vs 3.4062 (Table 6, rows 1-2). A normalization choice at fixed size shifts loss by about 0.026 nats.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed parameter count, normalization placement (pre- vs post-norm) changes pretraining loss only slightly.

record.problems: Only two parameter scales are compared for the model-size results; the study does not fit a power law or report uncertainty estimates. The matched-parameter architecture comparisons cover a limited set of variants.
record.rows_left_out: Table 5's separate domain and average values are included in r01–r22. Other training, downstream-task and kernel-efficiency comparisons were left out because they do not measure the claimed loss-scaling laws. Table 3 and Table 6 results for parameter-count-mismatched variants were not included for V4, which specifies fixed parameter count.

untested.parts: All of it: no power-law fit, no sweep over parameters, tokens or compute across orders of magnitude.
All of it: no depth/width sweep at fixed parameter count. The 48-layer and 24-layer models differ in parameter count (123M vs 71M).
All of it: downstream scores are reported only at two sizes, as method comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader tagged this study as tests/T2 on the strength of a two-size comparison and own-method rows. It should be cites_only/T6, with no verdicts.

versions.untested_parts: The power-law functional form, several orders of magnitude, and token- or compute-scaling sweeps are not tested; only 700M versus 1.5B at 400B training tokens is reported.
A broad range of widths, depths, and architecture choices at fixed parameter count is not tested.
